_workspace_root: NOT a config key — pass --workspace-root, or run the daemon from inside the workspace. This lets one config file drive several daemons over different workspaces on the same machine.
_: Every key below can also be given as a CLI flag (--poll-interval, --repo, ...), and the CLI wins. Keys prefixed with _ are comments.
_repos: Allowlist of owner/repo; empty means every repo that requests a review. --repo replaces this list rather than extending it.
_operators: GitHub logins allowed to re-open a capped PR with a `alissa-review: re-enter +N` comment (N up to 5). Empty means no ack is ever honoured; the reviewer identity is never an operator. --operator replaces this list rather than extending it.
_reviewer_login: The GitHub login every verdict must be posted under. null auto-detects it from the gh credential at startup. Either way the daemon re-checks the login before every review it submits and refuses to post as anyone else.
_reviewer_token_env: NAME of the environment variable holding the reviewer identity's GitHub token — never the token itself. Set it and every `gh` call runs under that credential explicitly, with the inherited GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN stripped. Leave it null and the daemon inherits whatever the process was given, and warns at startup: on a host that holds more than one GitHub identity, inheritance is how a round's verdict ends up posted under the wrong login.
_state_path: Omit to default to <workspace-root>/.revloop/state.db, which keeps daemons on different workspaces from sharing a spawn ledger.
_on_missing_hub: 'skip' (default) or 'add' to run `alissa code workspace add`. 'add' requires a non-empty repos allowlist.
_reap_grace_seconds: How long a reviewer session must be idle AND quiet (no tmux activity) before the reap sweep kills it, and before a stale round reads it as dead rather than working. Long enough that a just-merged PR's reviewer can finish its in-session close-out, and REJECTED at or above the 90-minute stale-round window (it also gates the stale-round liveness probe, whose respawn branch it would otherwise make unreachable).
_reap_session_cap: Alarm threshold, not a capacity limit: more live reviewer sessions than this after a sweep and the daemon logs page-worthy. A healthy loop runs a couple of concurrent rounds.
_checks_wait_seconds: How long a round holds its APPROVE while the judged head's CI rollup is still running (or unreadable) before recording the verdict as a COMMENT instead. PER CONDITION WAITED ON: an unreadable hold that becomes a genuine pending one restarts the clock once, so the worst-case hold is twice this (the daemon reports both numbers) — an approve from the reviewer identity is the operator's merge cue, so it must mean reviewed AND green. A RED rollup never waits: it posts REQUEST_CHANGES leading with the failing check names. 0 means never hold (degrade on the first poll). Skipped/neutral contexts never block.
